events.region: La Salle; McMullen; Live Oak; Bee; Goliad; Webb; Duval; Jim Wells; Inland Kleberg; Inland Nueces; Inland San Patricio; Coastal Aransas; Inland Refugio; Coastal Kleberg; Coastal Nueces; Coastal San Patricio; Aransas Islands; Coastal Refugio; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south Texas, including the following areas,
Aransas Islands, Bee, Coastal Aransas, Coastal Kleberg, Coastal
Nueces, Coastal Refugio, Coastal San Patricio, Duval, Goliad,
Inland Kleberg, Inland Nueces, Inland Refugio, Inland San Patricio,
Jim Wells, Kleberg Islands, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen, Nueces
Islands and Webb.

* WHEN...Until noon CST today.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A widespread swath of 4-8 inch radar estimated rainfall amounts
have fallen across the southern Rio Grande Plains/Brush Country
today. An additional 1-3 inch rainfall amounts are forecast
through Monday evening, with isolated areas of greater than 4
inches. Any rainfall over this high rainfall corridor and storms
with 2-4 inch rainfall rates/training storms (especially across
the urban areas and poor drainage wars) will lead to additional
flooding concerns.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Edwards County in south central Texas...
Northwestern Kinney County in south central Texas...
Northeastern Val Verde County in south central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM CST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1154 PM CST, Emergency management reported flooding in the
advisory area. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 3 and 5 inches of rain have fallen.

area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Rocksprings, Loma Alta, Carta Valley, Vinegarone, Kickapoo Cavern
State Park, Devils River State Nat Area Del Norte, Devil's
Sinkhole State Natural Area, Devils River State Nat Area Big
Satan, Devils Shores and Pafford Crossing.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A strong system is expected to move through the area Sunday night
into Monday. Temperatures below freezing combined with snow levels
below 1,000 ft are indicative of snowfall for upper elevations.
Mid-level southeasterly flow suggests potential for White Pass to be
sheltered from much of the precipitation, but would allow for ample
moisture to make it into the Haines Borough, falling as snow at the
border. The winter storm watch will be upgraded to a winter storm
warning for the upper elevations of the Haines Highway near Haines
Customs, and replaced with a winter weather advisory for the Klondike
Highway near White Pass.

* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations of 8 to 12
inches possible.

* WHERE...The Haines Highway, near Haines Border Crossing.

* WHEN...From 3 AM to 6 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The upper elevations of the Haines Highway,
near Haines Customs. Snow levels will steadily increase from around
500 ft to 2000 ft by Monday evening.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW
at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to noon PST Monday. High tide is at 10:52 AM
at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.
